definitions: The oldest and largest of the three pyramids on the Giza plateau in Egypt, built as a tomb for the pharaoh Khufu around 2560 BCE from an estimated 2.3 million limestone and granite blocks, each weighing on average over two tons.
colloq. The only wonder of the ancient world still standing, and it has never once let anyone forget it.
example: The tour guide pointed at the pyramid and reminded the group that a monument this thiccc took twenty years and an entire kingdom's labor force to finish.
etymology: The Greeks named it after their word pyramis, possibly borrowed from an Egyptian term for the wheat cakes it resembled in shape. It held the record for tallest human-made structure on Earth for roughly 3,800 years, a record no wheat cake has ever come close to threatening.
caption: The Great Pyramid rises in sharp, sunlit angles from the Giza plateau, its stepped limestone courses stacking toward a single distant point.

socialCaptions.morning: Pyramid, Great Giza. 2.3 million blocks and not one of them apologizing for the size.
socialCaptions.afternoon: Tallest structure on Earth for 3,800 years. Nothing else in this dictionary can say that.
socialCaptions.evening: From the archives, Pyramid, Great Giza.
socialCaptions.reels: Twenty years. A kingdom's labor. One extremely thiccc tomb.
